Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer). → [LLM] Vulnerable LobeHub <=2.1.56 in Defender / Sentinel vulnerability inventory
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] LobeHub /webapi/proxy POST from scripted / non-browser User-Agent · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] LobeHub /webapi/proxy response reflects Clerk session cookie with Domain=lobehub.com · Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Article-specific behavioural hunt — [GHSA / CRITICAL] CVE-2026-54157: LobeHub: Unauthenticated SSRF in `/webapi/prox
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.

LobeHub /webapi/proxy POST from scripted / non-browser User-Agent AIDelivery High
Detects unauthenticated POST requests to LobeHub's CVE-2026-54157 SSRF endpoint (`/webapi/proxy`) issued by curl/wget/python/PowerShell clients. Legitimate traffic to this route comes from the LobeHub web UI inside a browser; CLI / library user-agents touching it are extremely likely to be exploitation attempts. Rationale: Article shows the working PoC is `curl -X POST ... https://app.lobehub.com/webapi/proxy` — the endpoint is reachable from CLI without any auth, so attacker traffic shape will always be scripted-client UA. The LobeHub web UI invokes this from in-browser JS, so any non-browser UA on this exact path is high-fidelity exploitation. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-xmwj-c75x-6346
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal synthetic monitoring (Datadog Synthetics, Pingdom, Site24x7) probing the proxy endpoint as a health-check
  • CI/CD release-validation scripts using curl/python-requests against staging LobeHub
  • Security team's own SSRF mitigation tests against patched instances
  • Third-party LobeHub SDKs / mobile apps that send a non-browser UA
Suppression filter
| where RequestClientApplication !has "DatadogSynthetics" and RequestClientApplication !has "Pingdom" and RequestClientApplication !has "Site24x7"
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full POST body and check whether the URL the attacker proxied targets internal IPs, cloud metadata (169.254.169.254), or returned a reflected Set-Cookie — those upgrade severity instantly. 2) Contain: block the source IP at the edge / WAF and, on the LobeHub side, confirm package version is >2.1.56 with the `checkAuth()` patch applied; if not, hot-patch by adding the auth wrapper or removing the route. 3) Hunt: pivot on `SourceIP` for additional `/webapi/proxy` POSTs, search Clerk auth logs for `__session` values that match any reflected cookie, and review egress from LobeHub server IP for unexpected outbound during the same window.
let suspicious_ua = dynamic(["curl","wget","python-requests","python-urllib","go-http-client","powershell","httpie","libwww","java/","axios","node-fetch","nuclei","ffuf","gobuster"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteUrl has "lobehub.com/webapi/proxy"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe","opera.exe","iexplore.exe","safari.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
let suspicious_ua = dynamic(["curl","wget","python-requests","python-urllib","go-http-client","powershell","httpie","libwww","java/","axios","node-fetch","nuclei","ffuf","gobuster"]);
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RequestURL has "/webapi/proxy"
| where RequestMethod =~ "POST"
| extend ua = tolower(RequestClientApplication)
| where ua has_any (suspicious_ua) or isempty(ua) or ua == "-"
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, SourceIP, DestinationHostName, RequestURL, RequestMethod, RequestClientApplication
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: LobeHub /webapi/proxy POST from Scripted / Non-Browser Client (CVE-2026-54157)
id: 7c8a3b91-2e4f-4b25-9c11-3d51a6e7d8f2
description: Detects POST requests to the unauthenticated LobeHub /webapi/proxy SSRF endpoint coming from CLI / library user-agents rather than browsers.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-xmwj-c75x-6346
author: SOC detection engineering
date: 2026/06/17
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1190
  - cve.2026.54157
logsource:
  category: webserver
detection:
  selection_uri:
    cs-uri-stem|contains: '/webapi/proxy'
    cs-method: 'POST'
  selection_ua:
    cs-User-Agent|contains:
      - 'curl/'
      - 'wget/'
      - 'python-requests'
      - 'python-urllib'
      - 'Go-http-client'
      - 'PowerShell'
      - 'HTTPie'
      - 'libwww'
      - 'Java/'
      - 'axios'
      - 'node-fetch'
      - 'Nuclei'
      - 'ffuf'
      - 'gobuster'
  condition: selection_uri and selection_ua
falsepositives:
  - Internal synthetic monitoring or release-validation pipelines hitting the proxy endpoint
level: high
source:nginx @http.url_details.path:/webapi/proxy @http.method:POST @http.useragent:(*curl* OR *wget* OR *python-requests* OR *python-urllib* OR *Go-http-client* OR *PowerShell* OR *HTTPie* OR *libwww* OR *Java\/* OR *axios* OR *node-fetch* OR *Nuclei* OR *ffuf* OR *gobuster*)
WEB

| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| where match(http_user_agent, "(?i)(curl|wget|python-requests|python-urllib|Go-http-client|powershell|httpie|libwww|java/|axios|node-fetch|nuclei|ffuf|gobuster)") OR http_user_agent="" OR http_user_agent="-"

LobeHub /webapi/proxy SSRF body targets internal IP or cloud-metadata endpoint AIReconnaissance High
Detects POST requests to LobeHub's `/webapi/proxy` whose body URL points at RFC1918 internal ranges, loopback, `169.254.169.254` (AWS IMDS), `metadata.google.internal`, `metadata.azure.com`, or `file://`. These are the canonical SSRF targets attackers will pivot to once they discover the unauthenticated proxy. Rationale: Article PoC explicitly demonstrates POST-body URL fetching, and the GHSA confirms the only filter is `ssrfSafeFetch` — which historically has been bypassed via DNS rebinding and IPv6 mapping. Attacker bodies hitting metadata/loopback are the canonical post-discovery move; legitimate URL-preview traffic targets public domains only. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-xmwj-c75x-6346
ATT&CKT1190 T1526 T1595.002
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Authorised pentest or bug-bounty researcher re-testing the SSRF fix
  • Internal red team exercise scoped to the LobeHub asset
  • Misconfigured client app accidentally sending an internal hostname in the URL preview
  • Security scanner (Nuclei, Burp) running an SSRF template in a maintenance window
Response runbook
1) Triage: extract the exact SSRF target URL from the POST body and the HTTP response code/size — non-zero bodies returning AWS metadata JSON (`AccessKeyId`, `SecretAccessKey`) is an active credential-theft incident. 2) Contain: block the source IP at the edge, rotate any IAM role credentials attached to the LobeHub Vercel/EC2 identity, and upgrade LobeHub to >2.1.56 immediately. 3) Hunt: pull all CloudTrail events for the role/instance within the SSRF window for new credential use, search for the same source IP attempting other `/webapi/*` paths, and review for `__session` / `__clerk_db_jwt` cookie reflection (UC3).

| where RequestMethod =~ "POST"
| where Message has_any (ssrf_patterns)
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, SourceIP, DestinationHostName, RequestURL, RequestMethod, RequestClientApplication, Message
| order by TimeGenerated desc

LobeHub /webapi/proxy response reflects Clerk session cookie with Domain=lobehub.com AIExploitation High
Detects the response-side signature of the CVE-2026-54157 cookie-injection chain: `/webapi/proxy` reflects an attacker-controlled `Set-Cookie` whose name matches Clerk's auth cookies (`__session`, `__clerk_db_jwt`, `__client_uat`) and whose `Domain=` is `lobehub.com`. This is the session-fixation primitive against logged-in users. Rationale: Article's second PoC is a direct demonstration: the proxy reflects upstream `Set-Cookie: __session=malicious;Domain=lobehub.com` verbatim — only `Content-Encoding` and `Content-Length` are stripped. Clerk's three documented cookies (`__session`, `__clerk_db_jwt`, `__client_uat`) being set on `lobehub.com` from the proxy route can only happen via this bug. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-xmwj-c75x-6346 • https://clerk.com/docs/security/cookies
ATT&CKT1539 T1606.001
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • LobeHub's own Clerk auth endpoints legitimately issuing these cookies (different path — `/api/auth/*`, not `/webapi/proxy`)
  • Misconfigured upstream the proxy is fetching that coincidentally sets unrelated cookies named similarly
  • QA / staging environment intentionally injecting test cookies via the proxy
Response runbook
1) Triage: capture the reflected cookie value and the source IP that triggered the response — note any victim browser IPs in adjacent `/webapi/proxy` interactions that may have stored the cookie. 2) Contain: invalidate Clerk sessions matching the reflected `__session` / `__clerk_db_jwt` values (Clerk Dashboard → Sessions → Revoke), block the source IP, and force `checkAuth()` patch via emergency LobeHub upgrade. 3) Hunt: pull Clerk audit logs for sign-ins that used the fixed cookie value, review subsequent privileged actions on those accounts, and search webserver logs for repeated proxy POSTs from referrer pages outside `app.lobehub.com` (CSRF stage).
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RequestURL has "/webapi/proxy"
| where Message has "Set-Cookie"
| where Message has_any ("__session","__clerk_db_jwt","__client_uat")
| where Message matches regex @"(?i)Domain=\.?lobehub\.com"
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, SourceIP, DestinationHostName, RequestURL, RequestMethod, RequestClientApplication, Message
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Self-hosted LobeHub node process making outbound to internal / metadata IP (post-exploit SSRF) AIActions on Objectives Medium
For organisations running the npm `@lobehub/lobehub` package (≤2.1.56) on their own hosts: detects the LobeHub node.js server process initiating outbound connections to RFC1918 ranges, loopback, or cloud-metadata endpoints — the host-side smoking gun of CVE-2026-54157 being exploited against a self-hosted instance. Rationale: Article flags the npm package `@lobehub/lobehub <=2.1.56` is affected, meaning self-hosted deployments running node.js are in scope. Article also confirms the proxy reaches Vercel's management plane — on customer deployments, the equivalent target is the IMDS / private network. Outbound from the LobeHub node process to RFC1918 or 169.254.169.254 is the host-side fingerprint. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-xmwj-c75x-6346 • https://www.npmjs.com/package/@lobehub/lobehub
ATT&CKT1526 T1552.005
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Node.js HTTP client legitimately calling internal microservices (Redis, internal API)
  • cloud-init / SSM Agent / IMDSv2 credential refresh from the same host (different process)
  • Container orchestrator probes from the node sidecar against link-local
  • Self-hosted LobeHub instance with a documented internal proxy/RAG backend at an RFC1918 address
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "healthcheck" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "--prometheus"
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the source host is running `@lobehub/lobehub` (check package.json / running process command line) and that the destination is not a known internal microservice. Pull the upstream WAF/proxy log for matching `/webapi/proxy` POSTs in the same time window. 2) Contain: isolate the LobeHub host, rotate any IAM role / service-account credentials reachable from its metadata endpoint, and upgrade to >2.1.56 before re-attaching to network. 3) Hunt: search cloud audit logs (CloudTrail / Azure Activity / GCP audit) for API calls using credentials originating from the LobeHub instance role within the SSRF window; review egress for the same node PID making subsequent calls.

Vulnerable LobeHub <=2.1.56 in Defender / Sentinel vulnerability inventory AIWeaponization High
Asset-level detection: surfaces hosts where Defender's vulnerability inventory has identified CVE-2026-54157 (LobeHub `@lobehub/lobehub` ≤2.1.56). Pairs the finding with internet-exposure metadata so SOC can prioritise externally-reachable instances first. Rationale: Article specifies affected versions: `npm:@lobehub/lobehub <=2.1.56`. CveId match plus version-range regex provides a definitive asset hit. Joining DeviceInfo for `IsInternetFacing` lets the SOC prioritise the public-facing instances that the unauthenticated SSRF can be exploited against without any pre-existing access. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-xmwj-c75x-6346 • https://www.npmjs.com/package/@lobehub/lobehub

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688

Crawl4AI Python process outbound to cloud-metadata IP 169.254.169.254 (SSRF exploitation) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects when the Crawl4AI Docker server process (python/uvicorn/gunicorn) reaches out to the AWS/Azure/GCP instance-metadata link-local IP 169.254.169.254 or its IPv6 equivalent. This is the high-value SSRF target the advisory calls out for /crawl, /md, /llm, /crawl/job, /llm/job, and /execute_js abuse. Rationale: 169.254.169.254 is the exact cloud-metadata endpoint named in the advisory's SSRF section, and the advisory blocks the IP in validate_webhook_url(). Crawl4AI ships as a Docker app run by python/uvicorn, so the parent-process predicate is a high-fidelity narrowing.
ATT&CKT1552.005 T1090
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate IMDS calls from the Crawl4AI container at startup for IAM-role token refresh (boto3/azure-identity SDKs)
  • Health-check probes from cloud-init or k8s downward-API readiness scripts that share the same Python venv
  • DevOps debugging a new Crawl4AI deployment manually curl'ing IMDS to validate the role binding
  • Sidecar containers (Datadog agent, FluentBit) sharing a network namespace with the Crawl4AI pod
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("boto3", "botocore", "azure.identity", "google.auth") and InitiatingProcessAccountName in ("root", "appuser"))
Response runbook
1. Triage: pull the InitiatingProcessCommandLine and confirm it is the Crawl4AI server (look for `crawl4ai`, `--host 0.0.0.0`, port 11235). Pull web-proxy/access logs for the same host ±5 min for inbound POST to /crawl, /md, /llm, /crawl/job, /llm/job, or /execute_js. Check the request body for IMDS URL or IPv6-mapped IPv4 patterns. 2. Contain: block egress from the Crawl4AI container to 169.254.169.254 via NetworkPolicy / SG rule; force IMDSv2 with hop-limit=1; rotate any IAM role credentials the instance held. Patch Crawl4AI to >=0.8.7 or set CRAWL4AI_API_TOKEN and CRAWL4AI_EXECUTE_JS_ENABLED=false. 3. Hunt: search CloudTrail for AssumeRole / sts calls from the instance role in the last 24h originating from non-AWS IPs (credential exfil); check DeviceProcessEvents for shell children of the same Python process; pivot on the source IP of the inbound HTTP request to find the attacker.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(24h)
| where RemoteIP in ("169.254.169.254", "fd00:ec2::254")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("python", "python3", "python3.10", "python3.11", "python3.12", "uvicorn", "gunicorn")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("crawl4ai", "crawl4ai_server", "crawl4ai-serve")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where DstIpAddr in ("169.254.169.254", "fd00:ec2::254")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("python", "uvicorn", "gunicorn") or ActingProcessCommandLine has "crawl4ai"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Path traversal in Crawl4AI /screenshot or /pdf output_path parameter AIExploitation High
Detects HTTP POST requests to the Crawl4AI /screenshot or /pdf endpoints carrying an output_path value with directory traversal (../), absolute paths outside /tmp/crawl4ai-outputs, or sensitive-target extensions/paths (/etc/, /root/, .ssh, cron.d). Maps directly to CWE-22 / CVSS 9.1 fix that added validate_output_path(). Rationale: The advisory explicitly names /screenshot, /pdf, output_path, the .. traversal sequence, and the /tmp/crawl4ai-outputs default dir. Matching on `output_path=` plus traversal tokens or sensitive Linux paths is article-specific and not generic LFI noise.
ATT&CKT1190 T1083
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate users with output_path containing literal '..' in a project name like 'crawl-test..2026' (rare)
  • Penetration testers / Burp scanner sweeps against the staging cluster
  • Internal Crawl4AI integration tests submitting fixtures from a CI runner
  • URL-encoded paths in non-malicious automated screenshot pipelines if devs use legacy clients
Response runbook
1. Triage: confirm the requested output_path resolves to a sensitive path (/etc/cron.d/, /root/.ssh/authorized_keys, /etc/passwd, /var/spool/cron). Cross-check src IP against threat-intel and recent auth events. Pull POST body if the WAF stores it. 2. Contain: block the source IP at the edge; quarantine the Crawl4AI host; run `find / -newer /tmp/crawl4ai-outputs -mmin -60` to inventory any files the process may have written outside its sandbox. Upgrade Crawl4AI to >=0.8.7 and set CRAWL4AI_OUTPUT_DIR. 3. Hunt: search DeviceFileEvents for any files written by python/uvicorn outside /tmp/crawl4ai-outputs in the last 7d; check for new SUID binaries, new cron entries, new SSH authorized_keys lines on the host; pivot src IP across other web logs to detect campaign reuse.

| where Timestamp > ago(24h)
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("/screenshot", "/pdf")
| where RemoteUrl has "output_path"
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("..", "%2e%2e", "/etc/", "/root/", "/var/spool/cron", ".ssh", "/proc/", "/.bashrc", "/.profile", "crontab")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, LocalIP
| order by Timestamp desc
let traversal = dynamic(["..", "%2e%2e", "/etc/", "/root/", "/var/spool/cron", ".ssh", "/.bashrc", "/proc/", "crontab"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(W3CIISLog | where TimeGenerated > ago(24h) | where csUriStem has_any ("/screenshot", "/pdf") | where csUriQuery has "output_path" | where csUriQuery has_any (traversal) | project TimeGenerated, Computer, cIP, csMethod, csUriStem, csUriQuery, csUserAgent, scStatus),
(CommonSecurityLog | where TimeGenerated > ago(24h) | where RequestURL has_any ("/screenshot", "/pdf") | where RequestURL has "output_path" | where RequestURL has_any (traversal) | project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, SourceIP, RequestMethod, RequestURL, RequestClientApplication),
(ImWebSession | where TimeGenerated > ago(24h) | where Url has_any ("/screenshot", "/pdf") | where Url has "output_path" | where Url has_any (traversal) | project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, HttpMethod, Url, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, HttpStatusCode)

Crawl4AI Python/uvicorn server spawns shell child (post-/execute_js RCE) AIInstallation High
Detects the Crawl4AI server process (python, uvicorn, gunicorn) directly spawning a shell or scripting interpreter (bash, sh, dash, zsh, cmd.exe, powershell.exe). This is the textbook execution signal after abuse of /execute_js (CWE-94) or the hook sandbox escape mentioned in the credits, since the Crawl4AI server has no legitimate reason to spawn an interactive shell. Rationale: Article calls out /execute_js arbitrary JavaScript execution (CWE-94, CVSS 8.1) and a hook sandbox escape via asyncio. A web/asyncio server has no legitimate need to spawn an interactive shell — the parent-child predicate captures the RCE outcome regardless of which sink vuln was used.
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1059.004 T1059.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Crawl4AI maintenance scripts in the container entrypoint calling /bin/sh to chmod or run health checks
  • Playwright/Chromium auxiliary binaries spawned via shell helpers during browser startup
  • DevOps `kubectl exec` into the container starting bash interactively for debugging
  • Python subprocess calls from legitimate Crawl4AI extension code (rare but documented in hooks)
Suppression filter
| where not (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/healthcheck", "chmod +x /usr/local/bin/crawl4ai", "playwright install"))
Response runbook
1. Triage: capture the child ProcessCommandLine — look for reverse-shell patterns (bash -i, /dev/tcp/, nc -e, python -c socket), curl|sh, base64 -d, or wget to attacker IP. Pull the proxy access log for the same host ±2 min and check for POST to /execute_js. 2. Contain: kill the Crawl4AI container; pull network captures of any outbound from the host since the spawn; disable /execute_js by setting CRAWL4AI_EXECUTE_JS_ENABLED=false in the redeploy. Rotate IAM/secrets the container had access to. 3. Hunt: search DeviceProcessEvents for the same parent spawning curl/wget/nc/python -c in the last 7d; search DeviceFileEvents for new files in /tmp, /dev/shm, /var/tmp written by python; check ASEPs / cron / systemd unit files for persistence; pivot src IP from the proxy log across all web tier logs.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(24h)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("python", "python3", "uvicorn", "gunicorn")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "crawl4ai"
| where FileName in~ ("bash", "sh", "dash", "zsh", "ksh", "cmd.exe", "powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, AccountName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("python", "uvicorn", "gunicorn") or ParentProcessCommandLine has "crawl4ai"
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("bash", "sh", "dash", "zsh", "ksh", "cmd.exe", "powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Unauthenticated access to Crawl4AI /monitor destructive endpoints AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects HTTP requests to Crawl4AI monitor router endpoints — particularly /monitor/actions/cleanup, /monitor/ws, and /monitor/jobs — which the advisory confirms were mounted WITHOUT the token_dep dependency on vuln <=0.8.6. Any successful access to these admin endpoints from non-mgmt IPs indicates exploitation of CWE-306. Rationale: Advisory explicitly names /monitor/actions/cleanup as a destructive endpoint that was reachable without auth on <=0.8.6. Matching the exact endpoint paths and excluding internal source IPs targets external exploitation while tolerating legitimate ops-tooling access from RFC1918.
ATT&CKT1190 T1485
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal monitoring dashboards / Grafana scrapers polling /monitor/stats on a schedule
  • Kubernetes liveness/readiness probes hitting /monitor/health
  • DevOps engineer hitting /monitor/actions/cleanup from a jumphost to free disk space
  • Authenticated authorized testers from an external pen-test scope
Response runbook
1. Triage: pull the source IP, UserAgent, and any X-Forwarded-For for the request. Check whether the request bore an Authorization header (proxy log must capture this). For /monitor/actions/cleanup specifically, validate which jobs were torn down in the Crawl4AI app log. 2. Contain: deploy a WAF rule blocking /monitor/* from any IP outside the management CIDR until the host is upgraded to >=0.8.7 (which adds Depends(token_dep)). Rotate CRAWL4AI_API_TOKEN. 3. Hunt: query the same source IP across all web logs for /screenshot path-traversal, /crawl with IMDS URLs, or POST /execute_js — operators chaining the monitor recon with another vuln; check for any /monitor/ws WebSocket upgrades to spot persistent exfiltration channels.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(24h)
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("/monitor/actions/cleanup", "/monitor/ws", "/monitor/jobs", "/monitor/stats")
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
let mon_paths = dynamic(["/monitor/actions/cleanup", "/monitor/ws", "/monitor/jobs", "/monitor/stats", "/monitor/health"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(W3CIISLog | where TimeGenerated > ago(24h) | where csUriStem in (mon_paths) | where scStatus in (200, 101) | project TimeGenerated, Computer, cIP, csMethod, csUriStem, csUserAgent, scStatus),
(CommonSecurityLog | where TimeGenerated > ago(24h) | where RequestURL has_any (mon_paths) | where DeviceAction != "deny" | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, RequestMethod, RequestURL, RequestClientApplication, DeviceAction),
(ImWebSession | where TimeGenerated > ago(24h) | where Url has_any (mon_paths) | where HttpStatusCode in (200, 101) | project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, HttpMethod, Url, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, HttpStatusCode)
| where not(ipv4_is_private(tostring(coalesce(cIP, SourceIP, SrcIpAddr))))

Crawl4AI SSRF via IPv6-mapped IPv4 bypass pattern in /crawl, /md, /llm request AIExploitation High
Detects the exact SSRF bypass the advisory calls out by name: IPv6-mapped IPv4 addresses like `[::ffff:169.254.169.254]`, `[::ffff:10.0.0.1]`, `[::ffff:127.0.0.1]` sent to Crawl4AI's /crawl, /crawl/stream, /md, /llm, /crawl/job, /llm/job endpoints to evade naive hostname-string blocklists. Rationale: Article literally calls out `[::ffff:169.254.169.254]` and `[::ffff:10.0.0.1]` as the IPv6-mapped IPv4 bypass for the SSRF blocklist. The `::ffff:` token plus the named endpoints is a near-zero-FP signature.
ATT&CKT1190 T1090 T1027
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security research / Burp scanner with pre-canned SSRF payloads (often known via test-org headers)
  • IPv6 dual-stack logging tooling that legitimately embeds ::ffff: for client identity (extremely rare in URL payload)
  • Crawl4AI integration tests that include the bypass as a regression-test fixture
Response runbook
1. Triage: extract the embedded IPv6-mapped IPv4 address — normalize to its v4 form and check whether it targets 169.254.169.254 (IMDS), 127.0.0.1 / loopback, or RFC1918 internal services. Pull any 200 response: that means the SSRF succeeded. 2. Contain: block the src IP at the edge; force upgrade to Crawl4AI >=0.8.7 (advisory fix normalizes ::ffff: before blocklist check); ensure IMDSv2 hop-limit=1 on the host. 3. Hunt: pivot src IP across all web logs for other SSRF payloads (file://, gopher://, schemes), check DeviceNetworkEvents for any outbound from the Crawl4AI process to the normalized target IP, and rotate any creds reachable from the inside-perimeter target.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(24h)
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("/crawl", "/md", "/llm")
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("::ffff:", "%3A%3Affff%3A", "[::ffff:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
let bypass_tokens = dynamic(["::ffff:", "%3A%3Affff%3A", "[::ffff:"]);
let endpoints = dynamic(["/crawl", "/crawl/stream", "/md", "/llm", "/crawl/job", "/llm/job"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(W3CIISLog | where TimeGenerated > ago(24h) | where csUriStem has_any (endpoints) | where csUriQuery has_any (bypass_tokens) | project TimeGenerated, Computer, cIP, csMethod, csUriStem, csUriQuery, scStatus),
(CommonSecurityLog | where TimeGenerated > ago(24h) | where RequestURL has_any (endpoints) | where RequestURL has_any (bypass_tokens) | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, RequestMethod, RequestURL, RequestClientApplication),
(ImWebSession | where TimeGenerated > ago(24h) | where Url has_any (endpoints) | where Url has_any (bypass_tokens) | project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, HttpMethod, Url, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, HttpStatusCode)

Crawl4AI writes file outside /tmp/crawl4ai-outputs (output_path traversal landing) AIInstallation Medium
Detects Crawl4AI server process writing to filesystem locations OTHER than CRAWL4AI_OUTPUT_DIR's default `/tmp/crawl4ai-outputs`. This is the on-host landing signal that the /screenshot or /pdf path-traversal succeeded — it catches the file-write side regardless of how the web request was logged. Rationale: Article specifies CRAWL4AI_OUTPUT_DIR=/tmp/crawl4ai-outputs as the sanctioned write path for /screenshot and /pdf, and the fix restricts writes to that directory. Any write by python/uvicorn into /etc, /root, .ssh, cron, or /usr/local/bin is the post-traversal landing.
ATT&CKT1083 T1546 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Container entrypoint scripts run by python that copy config into /etc/crawl4ai/ at startup
  • pip install / package post-install hooks writing into /usr/local/bin (during deployment, not steady-state)
  • Playwright browser auto-update writing into ~/.cache
  • Backup scripts running as python wrappers
Suppression filter
| where not (FolderPath startswith "/etc/crawl4ai/" and ActionType == "FileCreated" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("setup.py", "pip install", "entrypoint"))
Response runbook
1. Triage: capture the full TargetFilePath and FileSize; hash the file (SHA256) and submit to VT/private sandbox. Check whether the file content matches the source of /screenshot or /pdf rendering (PNG/PDF magic bytes) — a real attack will write a webshell/cron/SSH key, not a PNG. 2. Contain: quarantine the file; kill the Crawl4AI container; if a cron or SSH key was written, expire it and rotate keys. Upgrade to Crawl4AI >=0.8.7 to inherit validate_output_path() + Pydantic field_validator. 3. Hunt: search proxy logs ±30 min for POST to /screenshot or /pdf with output_path; review DeviceProcessEvents for any new processes the dropped file spawned; pivot via the file hash across the fleet.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(24h)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated", "FileModified")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("python", "python3", "uvicorn", "gunicorn")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "crawl4ai"
| where not(FolderPath startswith "/tmp/crawl4ai-outputs" or FolderPath startswith "/tmp/playwright" or FolderPath startswith "/tmp/.cache")
| where FolderPath startswith "/etc/"
    or FolderPath startswith "/root/"
    or FolderPath startswith "/var/spool/cron"
    or FolderPath has "/.ssh/"
    or FolderPath startswith "/usr/local/bin/"
    or FolderPath has "/.bashrc"
    or FolderPath has "/.profile"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated", "FileModified")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("python", "uvicorn", "gunicorn") or ActingProcessCommandLine has "crawl4ai"
| where TargetFilePath !startswith "/tmp/crawl4ai-outputs"
| where TargetFilePath startswith "/etc/"
    or TargetFilePath startswith "/root/"
    or TargetFilePath startswith "/var/spool/cron"
    or TargetFilePath has "/.ssh/"
    or TargetFilePath startswith "/usr/local/bin/"
    or TargetFilePath has "/.bashrc"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType, TargetFilePath, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername

Crawl4AI /crawl/job or /llm/job webhook URL targets RFC1918 / metadata host (webhook SSRF) AIExploitation Medium
Detects POST submissions to Crawl4AI /crawl/job or /llm/job whose webhook URL parameter points at RFC1918, loopback, link-local cloud-metadata IPs/hostnames, or the IPv6-mapped IPv4 bypass. This is the CWE-918 / CVSS 8.6 vector and the fix added validate_webhook_url() at both job submission and send time. Rationale: Article names webhook URLs in /crawl/job and /llm/job, the 169.254.169.254 IMDS IP, RFC 1918 ranges, loopback, and link-local. These literal tokens in a single endpoint set form a precise CWE-918 signature.
ATT&CKT1190 T1552.005
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal CI/CD pipelines posting jobs with a corporate-internal webhook (RFC1918 by design)
  • Local-dev / staging environments where Crawl4AI calls back to a colocated worker at 10.x.x.x
  • Pen-testers running a documented engagement against the prod environment
Response runbook
1. Triage: extract the full webhook URL from the request body — categorize whether the target is IMDS (credential theft) vs RFC1918 (lateral discovery). Check the Crawl4AI app log for whether the job actually fired the webhook (advisory's fix added validation at SEND time, but old versions sent it). 2. Contain: block the src IP at the edge; upgrade Crawl4AI to >=0.8.7 (validate_webhook_url + follow_redirects=False); rotate any IAM creds reachable via IMDS if 169.254.169.254 was the target. 3. Hunt: cross-reference src IP with other /crawl, /md, /llm SSRF attempts and /monitor unauth-access; check the Crawl4AI process's DeviceNetworkEvents for any outbound to the webhook target post-job-creation; review CloudTrail for AssumeRole calls using the instance role from non-AWS sources.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(24h)
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("/crawl/job", "/llm/job")
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("169.254.169.254", "metadata.google.internal", "127.0.0.1", "localhost", "::ffff:", "://10.", "://192.168.", "://172.16.", "://172.17.", "://172.18.", "://172.19.", "://172.2", "://172.3")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP
| order by Timestamp desc

let endpoints = dynamic(["/crawl/job", "/llm/job"]);
union isfuzzy=true

Crawl4AI CVE-2026-53753: POST /crawl body with AST sandbox-escape payload (gi_frame/f_back/f_builtins) AIExploitation High
Hunts inbound POST requests to a Crawl4AI /crawl endpoint whose body contains the AST sandbox-escape payload (gi_frame/f_back/f_builtins/__import__) inside a JsonCssExtractionStrategy schema. Zero benign Crawl4AI traffic should reference Python frame/generator dunder-adjacent attributes — single high-fidelity exploit signature for CVE-2026-53753. Rationale: Article explicitly names gi_frame, f_back, f_builtins, __import__, and JsonCssExtractionStrategy as the exact chain abused by CVE-2026-53753. Cross-checked GHSA-qxjp-w3pj-48m7 advisory; payload tokens are not part of any legitimate Crawl4AI API contract so FP rate is near-zero on the right path. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-qxjp-w3pj-48m7 • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-53753
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.006
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal red-team / authorised pentest validation of the same CVE
  • Vendor or community PoC traffic against a deliberately exposed dev instance
  • Security scanner fingerprinting (Nuclei/Nessus once a CVE-2026-53753 template ships)
  • Developer fuzzing the /crawl endpoint with sample payloads found in the advisory
Suppression filter
| where SourceIP !in (dynamic(["<pentest_subnet>","<vuln_scanner_ip>"]))
| where SourceUserName !in~ ("redteam-svc","appsec-scan")
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: Pull the full POST body, request headers, and source IP for the matched event. Identify whether the Crawl4AI container/service responded with HTTP 200 and whether subsequent outbound connections (DNS, HTTP) from the container followed within 60 seconds. Check container/host process events for `python` spawning `sh`/`bash` after the request. 2) CONTAIN: If the request was successful, isolate the container/host, block the source IP at the WAF/edge, rotate any secrets reachable from the container (cloud metadata creds, env vars, API tokens). Upgrade crawl4ai > 0.8.6 or set `CRAWL4AI_API_TOKEN` immediately. 3) HUNT: Pivot on the source IP and User-Agent across other internet-exposed services for the last 30 days. Search the Crawl4AI host for new persistence (cron, systemd units), reverse-shell child processes, and outbound connections to attacker infrastructure.
let payload_signatures = dynamic(["gi_frame","f_back","f_builtins","__import__","JsonCssExtractionStrategy"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemotePort in (8000, 8001, 11235, 80, 443)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python.exe","python3.exe","uvicorn.exe","gunicorn.exe","crawl4ai.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("crawl4ai","crawl4ai.server","uvicorn")
| extend AdditionalFieldsParsed = parse_json(AdditionalFields)
| where tostring(AdditionalFieldsParsed) has_any (payload_signatures)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, LocalIP, LocalPort, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, AdditionalFields
| order by Timestamp desc

    | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, SourceUserName, RequestURL, RequestMethod, RequestClientApplication, Message, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct;
let AsimHits = ImWebSession

description: Detects inbound POST requests to a Crawl4AI /crawl endpoint whose body or query string contains Python generator/frame attributes used in the CVE-2026-53753 AST sandbox escape.

(source:nginx OR source:apache OR source:azure.appservice OR source:aws.alb) @http.method:POST @http.url_details.path:*\/crawl* (@http.url_details.queryString:(*gi_frame* OR *f_back* OR *f_builtins* OR *__import__* OR *JsonCssExtractionStrategy*) OR @http.useragent:(*gi_frame* OR *f_back* OR *f_builtins*))

Crawl4AI/uvicorn (python) parent spawning shell or reconnaissance binaries (post-RCE CVE-2026-53753) AIInstallation High
Hunts post-exploitation activity from CVE-2026-53753 by detecting Crawl4AI/uvicorn/gunicorn Python parents spawning shells (sh, bash, dash) or reconnaissance utilities (curl, wget, nc, whoami, id, uname). This is the canonical post-RCE process-tree footprint for a sandbox-escape that lands inside the Crawl4AI Docker container. Rationale: Article describes 'unauthenticated remote code execution inside the Docker container' with the ability to 'execute arbitrary system commands'. The Python/uvicorn → shell/recon child chain is the canonical post-RCE telemetry footprint and would not occur during normal Crawl4AI request handling. Cross-checked GHSA-qxjp-w3pj-48m7. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-qxjp-w3pj-48m7 • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/006/
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1059.006 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Container entrypoint scripts that legitimately exec curl/wget for health checks (e.g. wait-for-it.sh)
  • Developer SSH/exec into the running container running `whoami`/`id` interactively
  • Crawl4AI plugins that legitimately shell out to external scrapers (rare but possible)
  • Build-stage commands (pip install, pytest) leaking into runtime parent — filtered by exclusion list
  • CI/CD container test harnesses that invoke recon tools as part of smoke tests
Suppression filter
| where not(InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("healthcheck","wait-for-it","dockerize"))
| where not(ProcessCommandLine has_any ("--version","-V"))
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: Pull the full child command line and any subsequent process tree for the host. Confirm the parent is actually the Crawl4AI service (check PID-tree back to the container init / uvicorn worker). Cross-check inbound network events at the same Timestamp for POST /crawl traffic with the gi_frame/f_back signature. 2) CONTAIN: Isolate the host or kill the container. Block source IP at the WAF/edge. Snapshot the container filesystem for forensics before destroying. Rotate any secrets reachable from the container (cloud-metadata IAM creds, env-var API tokens, mounted secrets). Upgrade crawl4ai > 0.8.6 and set `CRAWL4AI_API_TOKEN`. 3) HUNT: Search 30 days back for the same parent→child shape across all internet-facing Python services. Sweep for newly-created cron entries, systemd units, SSH authorized_keys, and outbound connections to attacker C2 from this host. Block the source-IP/UA cluster across the perimeter.
let crawl4ai_parents = dynamic(["python","python.exe","python3","python3.10","python3.11","python3.12","uvicorn","uvicorn.exe","gunicorn"]);
let recon_children = dynamic(["sh","bash","dash","zsh","ash","curl","wget","nc","nc.exe","ncat","netcat","socat","whoami","whoami.exe","id","uname","hostname","hostname.exe","ifconfig","ip","ipconfig.exe"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (crawl4ai_parents)
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("crawl4ai","uvicorn","server","11235","app:app")
| where FileName in~ (recon_children)
| where not(InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("pip install","setup.py","pytest","jupyter","pre-commit","build"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc

Crawl4AI post-RCE credential-file, /proc/self/environ, or cloud-metadata access AIActions on Objectives High
Hunts post-exploitation reconnaissance from CVE-2026-53753 by detecting Crawl4AI/Python descendants reading credential files (/etc/passwd, /etc/shadow), process env (/proc/self/environ, printenv), or cloud instance-metadata (169.254.169.254). This is the canonical 'land and loot' footprint inside the Crawl4AI Docker container. Rationale: Article states impact is 'execute arbitrary system commands, read/write files, and exfiltrate secrets' inside the Docker container. Combined with MITRE T1552.001 listed in the kill-chain, the credential-file / /proc/self/environ / cloud-metadata access pattern is the canonical post-RCE looting fingerprint. Cross-checked GHSA-qxjp-w3pj-48m7 and MITRE T1552.005 (cloud instance metadata). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-qxjp-w3pj-48m7 • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1552/001/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1552/005/
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1552.005 T1083 T1082
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Compliance / vuln-scan agents inside the container reading /etc/passwd as part of CIS benchmarks
  • Container entrypoint or init scripts that render env vars via printenv for templating
  • Developer interactive sessions exec'ing into the container to inspect environment
  • K8s/EKS pod-identity sidecar containers that legitimately query 169.254.170.2 / 169.254.169.254
  • Cloud-init or AWS SDK initialisation in a freshly-started Python service (filter on parent chain to Crawl4AI specifically)
Suppression filter
| where not(InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("cis-benchmark","compliance-scan","cloud-init","aws-sdk-init"))
| where not(AccountName in~ ("sre-audit","compliance-svc"))
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: Pull the full command line, parent process tree, and Crawl4AI request log for the host within ±5 minutes. Confirm the parent chain traces back to the Crawl4AI service (uvicorn worker / app:app). Inspect outbound network events for exfiltration to attacker infrastructure. 2) CONTAIN: Treat any compromised cloud-metadata token as exposed — IMMEDIATELY rotate the IAM role/instance-profile credentials, revoke active sessions (STS), and force re-issue any service tokens mounted into the container. Isolate the container/host. Upgrade crawl4ai > 0.8.6, enable `CRAWL4AI_API_TOKEN`, and restrict /crawl to internal networks. 3) HUNT: Search CloudTrail/Activity logs for usage of the stolen IAM role from unfamiliar IPs over the last 30 days. Sweep all Crawl4AI hosts for the same parent→secret-read pattern. Search for new outbound connections from this container to non-corporate destinations.
let crawl4ai_lineage = dynamic(["python","python.exe","python3","python3.10","python3.11","python3.12","uvicorn","uvicorn.exe","gunicorn","sh","bash","dash","zsh"]);
let secret_markers = dynamic(["/etc/passwd","/etc/shadow","/proc/self/environ","printenv","169.254.169.254","/latest/meta-data","metadata.google.internal","169.254.170.2",".aws/credentials",".ssh/id_rsa",".kube/config",".docker/config.json"]);
let ProcHits = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (crawl4ai_lineage)
         or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ (crawl4ai_lineage)
    | where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("crawl4ai","uvicorn","server","11235","app:app")
         or ProcessCommandLine has_any (secret_markers)
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any (secret_markers)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
              ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
              ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              ChildImage = FolderPath,
              ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine;
let NetHits = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where RemoteIP in ("169.254.169.254","169.254.170.2","100.100.100.200")
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (crawl4ai_lineage)
         or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ (crawl4ai_lineage)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName,
              ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
              ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              ChildImage = "network",
              ChildCmd = strcat("net:", RemoteIP, ":", tostring(RemotePort));
union ProcHits, NetHits
| order by Timestamp desc
let crawl4ai_lineage = dynamic(["python","python3","python3.10","python3.11","python3.12","uvicorn","gunicorn","sh","bash","dash","zsh"]);
let secret_markers = dynamic(["/etc/passwd","/etc/shadow","/proc/self/environ","printenv","169.254.169.254","/latest/meta-data","metadata.google.internal","169.254.170.2",".aws/credentials",".ssh/id_rsa",".kube/config"]);
let ProcHits = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ActingProcessName has_any (crawl4ai_lineage) or ParentProcessName has_any (crawl4ai_lineage)
    | where ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("crawl4ai","uvicorn","server","11235","app:app")
         or TargetProcessCommandLine has_any (secret_markers)
    | where TargetProcessCommandLine has_any (secret_markers)
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
              ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine,
              TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, _ResourceId;
let NetHits = ImNetworkSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where DstIpAddr in ("169.254.169.254","169.254.170.2","100.100.100.200")
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkProtocol, DstHostname, _ResourceId;
union isfuzzy=true ProcHits, NetHits
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Multiple JetBrains IDE plugins caught stealing AI keys

Aikido
2026-06-16 8 use cases 3 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

A coordinated campaign of at least 15 JetBrains IDE plugins, published under seven vendor accounts, exfiltrates the AI provider API key you paste into their settings. Category: Vulnerabilities & Threats

ATT&CKT1176 T1190 T1195.002
IPs39.107.60.51

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Malicious JetBrains Marketplace plugin ID present in IDE plugins folder · Suspicious browser extension installation
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] JetBrains IDE process connects to malicious plugin C2 39.107.60.51 · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Inspected HTTP POST to /api/software/ with attacker's static X-Api-Key header · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
JetBrains IDE process connects to malicious plugin C2 39.107.60.51 AICommand & Control Medium
JetBrains IDEs run plugins inside the IDE's JVM, so a direct outbound connection from idea64.exe / pycharm64.exe / java.exe to the hardcoded attacker IP 39.107.60.51 is a high-fidelity indicator that one of the 15 malicious AI-assistant plugins has just exfiltrated a stored AI provider API key. The IP is single-purpose and sits in Alibaba Cloud (AS37963) with no legitimate use case for a developer endpoint. Rationale: 39.107.60.51 is the hardcoded plaintext-HTTP exfil server named verbatim in the Aikido write-up (Block 3 / IoC list). A single hit from a developer endpoint is sufficient — no other legitimate caller has been observed for this address.
ATT&CKT1041 T1567.002
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel researcher manually probing the C2 from a sandboxed dev VM
  • Outbound proxy / firewall liveness check explicitly configured to ping the published IOC
  • Sinkhole / decoy traffic from a deliberate honeypot deployment
  • Defender / EDR re-detonation of an archived malicious plugin during retro-hunt
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory / file-event history for the affected host and list every plugin under %APPDATA%\JetBrains\<IDE>\plugins — flag any whose XML plugin id matches the 15 IoCs (org.sm.yms.toolkit, com.json.simple.kit, etc.). Capture the InitiatingProcessAccountUpn — that user typed at least one AI provider API key into the plugin settings. 2) Contain: immediately revoke and rotate any OpenAI / DeepSeek / SiliconFlow API keys belonging to the user; uninstall the offending plugin and remove its directory; block 39.107.60.51 at the egress proxy. 3) Hunt: pivot on plugin id across all developer endpoints (DeviceFileEvents FolderPath has 'JetBrains' and 'plugins'); check OpenAI / DeepSeek billing portals for unusual usage in the last 60 days from unfamiliar IPs.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP == "39.107.60.51"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessAccountUpn, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, Protocol
| order by Timestamp desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DstIpAddr == "39.107.60.51"
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, SrcUsername, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkProtocol, Url, EventVendor, EventProduct
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Inspected HTTP POST to /api/software/ with attacker's static X-Api-Key header AIActions on Objectives Medium
Where a TLS-inspecting proxy or web gateway records full request URLs and headers, this catches the actual exfil call — POST http://39.107.60.51/api/software/<name> carrying the hardcoded static token X-Api-Key: F48D2AA7CF341F782C1D and a JSON body containing the victim's apiKey field. This is the most precise rule possible against the campaign because both the URL path and the token are unique to the malicious plugin codebase. Rationale: Both the URI path /api/software/ AND the destination 39.107.60.51 are taken verbatim from the deobfuscated save() handler in the article (Block 2). Either signal alone is unique to this campaign; together they leave no plausible false positive.
ATT&CKT1567 T1071.001
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal pentester replaying the published IOC against a sanctioned target
  • Threat-intel platform retrospectively decoding archived sandbox PCAPs
  • Vendor security scanner generating synthetic exfil traffic for control validation
  • Honeypot infrastructure deliberately calling the IOC
Response runbook
1) Triage: extract SourceIP / InitiatingProcessAccountUpn from the POST — that user's stored AI keys are already at the attacker. Identify which JetBrains IDE process (idea64.exe / pycharm64.exe / java.exe) made the call so the responsible plugin id can be tied back via plugin XML. 2) Contain: revoke and rotate every AI provider key (OpenAI / DeepSeek / SiliconFlow) associated with that developer; uninstall the offending plugin directory and clear the plugin's settings file; block 39.107.60.51 and any URI containing /api/software/ at the egress proxy. 3) Hunt: search 90 days of proxy logs for any prior POST to the same URI; pivot on the static header value 'F48D2AA7CF341F782C1D' in raw proxy capture if header logging is enabled; query AI provider billing dashboards for spend anomalies on the victim's keys.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP == "39.107.60.51" or RemoteUrl has "/api/software/"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountUpn, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl
| order by Timestamp desc
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DestinationIP == "39.107.60.51" or RequestURL has "/api/software/"
| where RequestMethod =~ "POST"
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, SourceUserName, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, RequestMethod, RequestURL, RequestClientApplication, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Malicious JetBrains Marketplace plugin ID present in IDE plugins folder AIInstallation High
All 15 IoC plugin XML ids (org.sm.yms.toolkit, com.json.simple.kit, com.my.code.tools, ord.cp.code.ai.kit, etc.) are distinctive enough that any file write under %APPDATA%\JetBrains\<IDE>\plugins or ~/.config/JetBrains/<IDE>/plugins that contains one of these identifiers is conclusive evidence the host installed a backdoored plugin from the campaign. This catches the install moment regardless of whether the user has yet pasted an AI API key. Rationale: Plugin XML ids are the canonical, unique identifier JetBrains uses to dedupe Marketplace entries; the 15 ids in the article's IoC table are the verbatim package identifiers and will be present on disk in any installed copy (Marketplace install writes them into the plugin's META-INF). High-fidelity with effectively zero collision risk.
ATT&CKT1195.001 T1505.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Endpoint forensics tool re-reading a quarantined plugin artifact
  • Backup software touching the JetBrains plugins directory and re-emitting filenames
  • Developer manually examining a benign plugin coincidentally named identically (improbable — these ids are squatted attacker-chosen strings)
  • Security inventory scanner enumerating installed plugin metadata
Response runbook
1) Triage: enumerate every plugin under %APPDATA%\JetBrains (Win) or ~/Library/Application Support/JetBrains (mac) or ~/.config/JetBrains (Linux) on the host; cross-reference plugin.xml id against the 15 IoCs; pull DeviceNetworkEvents for that host to confirm whether 39.107.60.51 was already contacted (key already exfil'd). 2) Contain: uninstall the plugin via JetBrains Plugins UI (Disable → Restart → Remove), then delete the residual directory; rotate any AI provider API keys that user has used in the IDE in the last 90 days; push EDR-level block for the plugin id strings. 3) Hunt: sweep the entire developer fleet with the same query over 60d to find every infected host; cross-reference vendor accounts (CodePilot/mycode, StackSmith/misshewei, CodeCrafter/keteme, CodeWeaver/simpledev, JetCode/skyblue, DailyCode/dialycode, ZenCoder/947cb4c8-5db1-4cf0-8182-0aae7c433bb3) for any future plugin uploads.
let MaliciousPluginIds = dynamic(["org.sm.yms.toolkit","com.json.simple.kit","org.bug.find.tools","org.translate.ai.simple","com.yy.test.ai.simple","com.dev.ai.toolkit","com.json.view.simple","com.my.git.ai.kit","org.check.ai.ds","com.review.tool.code","org.code.assist.dev.tool","com.coder.ai.dpt","com.my.code.tools","ord.cp.code.ai.kit","com.dp.git.ai.tool"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(60d)
| where FolderPath has "JetBrains" and FolderPath has "plugins"
| where FileName has_any (MaliciousPluginIds) or FolderPath has_any (MaliciousPluginIds)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountUpn, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let MaliciousPluginIds = dynamic(["org.sm.yms.toolkit","com.json.simple.kit","org.bug.find.tools","org.translate.ai.simple","com.yy.test.ai.simple","com.dev.ai.toolkit","com.json.view.simple","com.my.git.ai.kit","org.check.ai.ds","com.review.tool.code","org.code.assist.dev.tool","com.coder.ai.dpt","com.my.code.tools","ord.cp.code.ai.kit","com.dp.git.ai.tool"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
| where TargetFilePath has "JetBrains" and TargetFilePath has "plugins"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (MaliciousPluginIds) or TargetFileName has_any (MaliciousPluginIds)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"

| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'

        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'

      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium

Google Vertex AI SDK Flaw Let Attackers Hijack Model Uploads via Bucket Squatting

The Hacker News
2026-06-16 10 use cases 4 techniques 7 kill-chain phases detected

A flaw in the Google Cloud Vertex AI SDK for Python let an attacker with no access to a victim's project hijack the victim's machine learning model upload and run code inside Google's serving infrastructure. Palo Alto Networks Unit 42, which found and reported the bug through Google's bug bounty program, calls the technique "Pickle in the Middle" and said it saw no exploitation in the wild.

Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer). → [LLM] Bucket Squatting: GCS bucket created matching Vertex AI predictable staging-name pattern
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Vertex AI model artifact written to *-vertex-staging-* bucket outside caller's project · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Race-condition pickle swap: rapid object overwrite in Vertex AI staging bucket within 5s · Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Vulnerable google-cloud-aiplatform SDK install (<1.148.0 - Pickle in the Middle exposure)
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
Bucket Squatting: GCS bucket created matching Vertex AI predictable staging-name pattern AIWeaponization High
Detects creation of Google Cloud Storage buckets that follow the Vertex AI SDK's predictable default staging-bucket naming convention ('<project>-vertex-staging-<region>'). Unit 42's 'Pickle in the Middle' attack pre-creates this exact bucket name in an attacker-controlled project so victim SDKs (google-cloud-aiplatform < 1.148.0) silently upload models to attacker-owned storage. Surfacing the squat at bucket-creation time catches the attack before any model is hijacked. Rationale: Anchors on the exact predictable bucket-name token 'vertex-staging-' the article cites as the SDK's pre-patch default ('project-vertex-staging-region'). Bucket-creation events are low-volume and a name carrying that token from any principal outside your own project ID is a hijack precursor with near-zero legitimate analog.
ATT&CKT1583.006 T1195.002
Data sourcesChange.All_Changes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Vertex AI itself auto-creating a legitimate default staging bucket for a freshly-provisioned project in a new region (caller is gcp-sa-aiplatform service agent of YOUR project)
  • Internal ML team manually creating a staging bucket using the same naming convention they saw in tutorials/docs
  • Terraform / Pulumi modules that bootstrap a Vertex AI workspace and pre-create the staging bucket
  • Re-creation of an existing staging bucket after a region migration or accidental delete
  • Vertex AI Workbench notebook instance initialization in a previously-unused region
Suppression filter
// Suppress if the bucket creator's project matches the embedded project in the bucket name
| where not (Application == "Google Cloud Platform" and AccountDisplayName has EmbeddedProject)
Response runbook
1. Triage: Extract the bucket-name embedded project ID and compare it to the creator's project ID (caller's gcp-sa-aiplatform service-agent project number, or IAM identity). If the embedded project belongs to YOUR org and the creator does not, you are looking at an active squat. Pull bucket IAM bindings — attacker squats are usually externally exposed. 2. Contain: File a Google Cloud abuse report against the squatting bucket for immediate takedown, and rotate any Vertex AI service-agent OAuth tokens that may have been exposed. Globally enforce `staging_bucket=` in all Vertex AI SDK invocations and pin google-cloud-aiplatform >= 1.148.0 in CI/CD requirements files. 3. Hunt: Search storage.objects.create within the squat bucket for the last 30 days — any objects in '.pkl', '.joblib', '.pb', or saved_model paths written by your service agents confirms model interception occurred. Pivot to BigQuery jobs.* and aiplatform.googleapis.com Model.upload audit logs for the same time window.
// Requires Defender for Cloud Apps GCP connector
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application has_any ("Google Cloud Platform","Google Cloud Storage","GCP")
| where ActionType has_any ("storage.buckets.create","BucketCreated","Insert bucket","google.storage.v1.Storage.CreateBucket")
| extend BucketName = tolower(coalesce(ObjectName, tostring(parse_json(tostring(RawEventData)).resourceName)))
| where BucketName matches regex @"vertex-staging-(us|europe|asia|northamerica|southamerica|me-|africa-)"
   or BucketName has "-vertex-staging-"
| extend EmbeddedProject = extract(@"^(.*?)-vertex-staging-", 1, BucketName)
| extend Region = extract(@"-vertex-staging-(.+)$", 1, BucketName)
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, AccountObjectId, AccountType, IPAddress, CountryCode, ISP, Application, ActionType, BucketName, EmbeddedProject, Region, RawEventData
| order by Timestamp desc
// Microsoft Sentinel — auto-derived from the Defender XDR hunt.
// Requires the Microsoft 365 Defender data connector (streams the
// advanced-hunting tables into Sentinel; Timestamp → TimeGenerated).
// Requires Defender for Cloud Apps GCP connector
CloudAppEvents
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Application has_any ("Google Cloud Platform","Google Cloud Storage","GCP")
| where ActionType has_any ("storage.buckets.create","BucketCreated","Insert bucket","google.storage.v1.Storage.CreateBucket")

   or BucketName has "-vertex-staging-"
| extend EmbeddedProject = extract(@"^(.*?)-vertex-staging-", 1, BucketName)
| extend Region = extract(@"-vertex-staging-(.+)$", 1, BucketName)
| project TimeGenerated, AccountDisplayName, AccountObjectId, AccountType, IPAddress, CountryCode, ISP, Application, ActionType, BucketName, EmbeddedProject, Region, RawEventData
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: GCS Bucket Squatting - Vertex AI Predictable Staging Name (Pickle in the Middle)
id: 7a3f4d2e-8b1c-4f5a-9d2e-3c4b5a6d7e8f
status: experimental
description: Detects creation of a Google Cloud Storage bucket whose name matches the Vertex AI Python SDK's predictable default staging-bucket pattern '<project>-vertex-staging-<region>'. This is the setup step for Unit 42's 'Pickle in the Middle' technique against google-cloud-aiplatform < 1.148.0.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/google-vertex-ai-sdk-flaw-let-attackers.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/19
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1583.006
  - attack.t1195.002
logsource:
  product: gcp
  service: gcp.audit
detection:
  selection_create:
    gcp.audit.method_name:
      - storage.buckets.create
      - google.storage.v1.Storage.CreateBucket
  selection_name:
    gcp.audit.resource_name|contains: 'vertex-staging-'
  condition: selection_create and selection_name
falsepositives:
  - Vertex AI legitimately auto-creating the default staging bucket for a new project/region (verify caller owns the embedded project ID)
  - Internal naming conventions that happen to include the literal 'vertex-staging' substring
level: high
source:gcp.audit (@protoPayload.methodName:storage.buckets.create OR @protoPayload.methodName:google.storage.v1.Storage.CreateBucket) (@protoPayload.resourceName:*vertex-staging-* OR @protoPayload.request.name:*vertex-staging-*)
CLOUD
